C08-M01-L04-F1.title: The analyst's shift: orient once, loop per alert, hand over
C08-M01-L04-F1.caption: An analyst reads the handover and checks SOC health once, repeats the pick-handle-document-decide loop for every alert, and ends the shift with a handover.
C08-M01-L04-F1.alt: Top-to-bottom diagram of seven steps: Read the handover; Check SOC health (log sources, intel, change calendar); Pick and acknowledge (highest priority, then oldest); Handle the alert (read rule, scope, enrich, validate, related alerts); Document as you go (UTC, exact queries, evidence references); Decide (close, keep investigating in the time box, or escalate now). From Decide a dashed loop arrow labelled next alert returns to Pick and acknowledge, and an arrow labelled shift ends leads to Write the handover.

nodes.label: Handle the alert
nodes.sub: read rule, scope, enrich, validate, related alerts

nodes.label: Decide
nodes.sub: close / keep investigating (time box) / escalate now

nodes.label: Write the handover
nodes.sub: becomes the next shift's first step

C08-M01-L04-F1.note: Orientation happens once per shift; the pick-handle-document-decide loop repeats for every alert.

C08-M01-L04-F2.title: Case notes: weak versus defensible
C08-M01-L04-F2.caption: The same investigative step on CASE-0001 recorded two ways; only the defensible note can be reproduced, reviewed and handed over.
C08-M01-L04-F2.alt: Two-column comparison. Weak note: 10:30 checked proxy, looks like beaconing; user probably opened something; escalated to T2. Defensible note: 2026-11-03 08:40Z, owner analyst.t1; query run: SELECT ... WHERE host='WS-104' AND url LIKE '%ping%'; fact: 18 requests of 220 bytes to cdn-telemetry-sync.example from 06:17Z; assessment (labelled): consistent with C2 beaconing; evidence: WS-104_2026-11-03_events.jsonl, SHA-256 8521c97c...; escalated to IR on-call via case system, acknowledged.
